entries.title: How ISVs are unlocking European workloads using Google Cloud Dedicated technology
entries.summary: Across Europe, organizations handling sensitive workloads in regulated sectors — such as financial services, healthcare, critical infrastructure, and the public sector — are trying to modernize their infrastructure while adhering to strict local data governance standards, including SecNumCloud in France and BSI C3A in Germany. To help organizations accomplish this, Google Cloud Dedicated provides
entries.content:
Mattia Tocco

Product Lead, Google Cloud Dedicated

Alfred Chung

Product Manager, Google Cloud Dedicated

Across Europe, organizations handling sensitive workloads in regulated sectors — such as financial services, healthcare, critical infrastructure, and the public sector — are trying to modernize their infrastructure while adhering to strict local data governance standards, including SecNumCloud in France and BSI C3A in Germany.

To help organizations accomplish this, Google Cloud Dedicated provides the architectural, security, and API consistency of Google Cloud in locally governed environments managed by independent domestic operators. But infrastructure is only the starting point. Organizations also need to transform the software ecosystem they rely on every day.

To meet regional sovereignty requirements, organizations acquire and run these software solutions through trusted local entities — such as S3NS in France (a joint venture majority-owned and managed by Thales) and a newly formed German entity that will also be owned and managed by Thales, currently in preview. These local entities operate dedicated infrastructure stacks, help maintain operational custody, and handle customer data within independent jurisdictional boundaries.

Today, we are highlighting the expanding independent software vendor (ISV) ecosystem validated on Google Cloud Dedicated, enabling French and German organizations to run their critical enterprise software in environments designed to support their sovereign and regulatory needs.

The local partner model: Cloud capability under domestic custody

Deploying in a sovereign boundary should not require an organization to sacrifice software choice or rewrite its enterprise applications.Because Google Cloud Dedicated provides architectural and API consistency with Google Cloud, validated enterprise software runs directly inside these partner-operated environments without custom re-platforming.

This model provides European enterprises with three concrete advantages:

  • Localized operational custody: Infrastructure operations, software quarantine procedures, and day-to-day administrative access are under the direct management of local European partners operating with specialized remote technical escalations governed by strict, partner-supervised escorted access controls.

  • Broad software choice: Regulated institutions can deploy industry-standard tools for identity governance, cyber resilience, simulation, and data streaming natively in their sovereign perimeter.

  • Streamlined compliance: Organizations fulfill national frameworks like SecNumCloud and BSI guidelines while preserving familiar CI/CD pipelines, APIs, and developer workflows.

Software choice is the true bottleneck for sovereign migrations

When highly regulated European institutions consider moving to a sovereign cloud, the infrastructure itself is rarely the primary roadblock. The real bottleneck is software.Historically, pursuing strict sovereignty meant accepting compromises:

  • Rewriting applications from scratch or maintaining custom, brittle tooling because mainstream enterprise platforms were unavailable.

  • Forcing security, engineering, and data teams to abandon the industry-standard tools they use daily in favor of untested niche alternatives.

  • Sidelining high-impact initiatives like real-time fraud scoring, automated DevSecOps, and modern identity governance simply because the required ISVs could not legally or technically operate in the environment.

Because Google Cloud Dedicated maintains architectural and API consistency with Google Cloud, leading global and European software providers can deploy their proven platforms directly inside national, domestic operator-managed boundaries. Regulated organizations retain the software, automated pipelines, and operational standards they rely on — without sacrificing compliance or operational custody.

Validated ISVs on Google Cloud Dedicated

Deploying enterprise software on Google Cloud Dedicated and S3NS isn't just about hosting an application locally; it’s about pairing proven software engines with sovereign operations. Here is how these joint architectures unlock strategic value for European enterprises:

  • Cohesity on Google Cloud Dedicated (Sovereign cyber resilience): Cohesity has many options to meet organizational data sovereignty objectives, whether on-premises or in the cloud with Google Cloud Dedicated. This is done through a unified, cyber resilient, AI-powered data platform — Cohesity Data Cloud — that is sovereign-by-design, making it easier to protect, manage, recover, and have visibility into data, while supporting compliance with data sovereignty requirements.

    For example, running Cohesity directly in the S3NS perimeter combines Cohesity’s Zero Trust cyber resilience architecture designed for immutability with local operational custody. Customers gain advanced threat hunting, cyber vaulting, and recovery orchestration that powers quick, clean, and trusted cyber-recovery from ransomware threats without allowing diagnostic telemetry, secondary backup copies, or operational keys to traverse external networks.

  • GitLab on Google Cloud Dedicated (Secure, compliant software delivery pipelines): Combining GitLab’s DevSecOps platform with Google Cloud Dedicated allows defense, aerospace, and public sector engineering teams to ship code at commercial velocity. Proprietary source code, vulnerability scans, and CI/CD artifact registries stay contained behind the partner-operated boundary, significantly reducing audit friction of using public SaaS code repositories.

  • Ansys, part of Synopsys, on Google Cloud Dedicated (High-performance sovereign engineering simulation): Pairing Ansys, part of Synopsys, high-performance computing simulation workflows with the dedicated compute clusters of Google Cloud Dedicated gives European manufacturers the massive scale needed for aerodynamic, fluid, and structural modeling. Highly sensitive intellectual property, blueprints, and digital twins designed to keep intellectual property within regional boundaries and national jurisdiction while running at cloud speed.

  • Memority on Google Cloud Dedicated / S3NS (Audit-ready sovereign identity governance): Integrating Memority’s identity factory platform directly into the S3NS SecNumCloud-qualified environment provides regulated entities with capabilities designed to support their NIS2 and DORA compliance requirements with the PREMI3NS SecNumCloud-qualified environment. Organizations can manage and audit millions of identities without building custom IAM infrastructure or exposing access tokens to non-European cloud services.

    "Our customers — from critical infrastructure operators to financial institutions — share the same requirement: an enterprise-grade IAM platform capable of managing millions of identities while meeting the highest standards of digital sovereignty. As NIS2 and DORA reshape the regulatory landscape, this requirement has become a business-critical imperative. S3NS enables us to address it at scale by providing a comprehensive IAM platform hosted in a SecNumCloud-qualified cloud environment, with built-in capabilities supporting the auditability, traceability, and operational resilience expected under these regulations,” said Francis Grégoire, Deputy CEO, Memority.

  • RackWare on Google Cloud Dedicated (De-risked cloud migration): Running RackWare’s automated migration and disaster recovery engines on Google Cloud Dedicated gives organizations a low-friction bridge from on-premises data centers into sovereign cloud environments. Teams can replicate, synchronize, and failover complex enterprise operating environments, bypassing the prohibitive cost and timeline of manual application refactoring.

  • Striim on Google Cloud Dedicated (Real-time data streaming without jurisdictional risk): Combining Striim’s continuous change data capture engine with the local boundaries of Google Cloud Dedicated enables organizations to feed live operational analytics and fraud models without batch delays. Financial institutions and logistics leaders can stream sensitive customer and payment transactions in sub-second intervals, with strong technical assurances that streaming pipelines remain bound to local infrastructure.

    "Regulated organizations should not have to choose between modern, real-time data and the control their environments demand. By making Striim available on Google Cloud Dedicated, we can help customers securely move and continuously deliver trusted data to the systems that power critical operations, analytics, and AI without ever compromising on sovereignty or resilience,” said Phillip Cockrell, SVP of Business Development, Striim.

    UPS Capital integrated Striim’s real-time streaming technology with analytics models to power its DeliveryDefense address verification and delivery security system. By streaming and validating transaction and delivery data continuously without batch lag, UPS assesses risk scoring in real time — a capability European logistics and financial operators can now deploy directly in their sovereign boundary.

  • Red Hat on Google Cloud Dedicated (Operational consistency on open hybrid platforms): Deploying Red Hat Enterprise Linux and OpenShift across Google Cloud Dedicated bridges on-premises infrastructure and sovereign cloud environments. Engineering teams maintain their existing operating runtimes, container standards, and administrative toolsets across sites, avoiding vendor lock-in and eliminating the operational retraining typically required when moving to sovereign stacks.

  • Saviynt on Google Cloud Dedicated (Zero-trust access governance across sovereign assets): Deploying Saviynt’s privileged access management and identity governance inside the sovereign boundary allows enterprises to centrally enforce least-privilege security across critical databases and workloads. Security administrators maintain automated role lifecycles and complete audit logs without exposing access intelligence to offshore management planes.

  • Tsuga on Google Cloud Dedicated (Telemetry and observability): Tsuga’s bring-your-own-cloud (BYOC) observability platform deployed inside a customer's dedicated VPC resolves one of the biggest security exposures in regulated IT: transmitting production telemetry to third-party SaaS monitoring providers. By processing all traces, metrics, and logs on local storage, organizations achieve full observability, reduce external data egress costs, and help protect sensitive operational data.

  • MongoDB on Google Cloud Dedicated (Modern data velocity with domestic residency): Running MongoDB Enterprise Advanced on Google Cloud Dedicated gives developers the flexibility of the document model while adhering to strict regional isolation requirements. Regulated organizations can rapidly build modern, real-time applications and customer portals using modern development patterns without being forced onto legacy relational database architectures.

  • Ispirer on Google Cloud Dedicated (Automated legacy modernization): Pairing Ispirer’s automated database conversion toolkit with Google Cloud Dedicated addresses a key friction point in database modernization: the complexity of migrating legacy database engines. Automated code and schema conversion shrinks complex multi-year migration timelines into predictable, low-risk deployments on modern sovereign infrastructure.

    "Every migration is really a risk decision. Offering the Ispirer toolkit on Google Cloud Dedicated gives customers over 27 years of deterministic conversion experience—that's the value we consistently hear back from client teams,” said Natallia Bespalova, CEO, Ispirer Systems.

  • Splunk integration with Google Cloud Dedicated (sovereign log collection, observability, and SIEM integration): Splunk now supports Google Cloud Dedicated as a first-class log source. Extensions to the open-source OpenTelemetry Collector allow organizations to export logs from Google Cloud Dedicated environments into Splunk Enterprise using the Google Cloud Pub/Sub receiver and the Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) exporter, alongside enhancements to the Splunk Add-on for Google Cloud for direct log collection Additionally, Splunk Observability Cloud now supports Google Cloud Dedicated through its Infrastructure Monitoring cloud integration, which connects projects to pull metrics and metadata from services so teams can monitor resource and application health. Critical infrastructure and financial institutions can now centralize security analytics, performance monitoring, SIEM operations, and incident response while keeping audit logs, threat intelligence, and sensitive operational telemetry within national boundaries. 

  • Solo.io on Google Cloud Dedicated (Kubernetes-native governance and runtime for AI agents): kagent from Solo.io adds a Kubernetes-native runtime for AI agents and their MCP tool servers on Google Cloud Dedicated, declared and governed through the same GitOps and RBAC workflows platform teams already operate. Lifecycle control, agent-level access policy, and human-in-the-loop approval are built in, helping organizations ensure agents are deployed, audited, and managed within the local partner perimeter.

  • Pelico on Google Cloud Dedicated (Sovereign supply chain resilience for aerospace and defense): Running Pelico on Google Cloud Dedicated with S3NS PREMI3NS gives industrial manufacturers the ability to turn ERP and planning data into clear operational priorities while keeping sensitive data under European sovereign control. Proven for a global aerospace and defense group, this architecture lets sovereignty-minded organizations anticipate and resolve supply chain disruptions using the capabilities of Pelico’s cloud offering, without compromising strict regional isolation or domestic operational custody.

Get started

To learn more about deploying validated software solutions within your sovereign perimeter:

  • For French organizations: Explore validated software and manage deployment options directly through S3NS.
  • For German organizations: Connect with your local partner team to review architecture patterns and BSI C5 and C3A compliance roadmaps.

entries.title: Inside the new Google Cloud Data Boundary experience
entries.summary: Digital sovereignty is evolving from a standard compliance requirement into a powerful strategic advantage for regulated industries worldwide. From European frameworks designed to meet sovereign standards (DORA, EHDS, GDPR) to FedRAMP/ILs/ITARs in the U.S., or expanding mandates across Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, organizations can build deeper global trust through clear governance over data
entries.content:
Nitin Garg

Engineering Director, Regulated Cloud

Ruchi Khurana

Group Product Manager, Regulated Cloud

Digital sovereignty is evolving from a standard compliance requirement into a powerful strategic advantage for regulated industries worldwide. From European frameworks designed to meet sovereign standards (DORA, EHDS, GDPR) to FedRAMP/ILs/ITARs in the U.S., or expanding mandates across Asia-Pacific and the Middle East, organizations can build deeper global trust through clear governance over data locality, encryption keys and system access.

Historically, achieving that level of control meant accepting an impossible tradeoff: rely on rigid legacy architectures that lacked access to frontier AI innovation, or stitch together brittle, manual guardrails that slowed developer velocity.

Google Cloud Data Boundary helps remove that compromise. Built directly onto Google Cloud’s global commercial infrastructure, Data Boundary delivers software-defined, AI-assisted governance. This allows organizations to move at commercial speed with verifiable sovereign controls built in from day one. Today, we’re announcing a new and updated experience in Data Boundary.

Google Cloud Data Boundary combines technical controls across residency, access, and encryption with ongoing monitoring and operational assurance.

What’s new in Data Boundary

Data Boundary streamlines how security, data and AI teams configure, test and scale governance across their cloud footprint. Below are the key highlights for the new experience:

  • End-to-end visibility into sovereign controls: Browse and deploy pre-configured regional and industry frameworks with clear visibility into mapped technical controls, severities and remediation steps.

  • Flexible hierarchy-wide enforcement: Apply preventative guardrails across organizations, complex nested folders and projects — on both net-new and existing workloads — to block out-of-policy API calls and configuration drift.

  • Dry run posture validation: Dry run any framework in monitor mode across live existing workloads to identify drift and violations before enabling active enforcement.

  • Compliance customization: Frameworks and controls customization according to your organization's needs. Use Gemini in Google Cloud to customize controls and generate remediation logic to help reduce manual compliance toil.

  • Accelerated compliance with machine-readable evidence: Continuously monitor posture, record immutable exception justifications, run scheduled audits and export machine-readable audit evidence to help fast-track certification workflows.

Turn compliance and digital sovereignty into a business accelerator

In an era of evolving global regulations and rapid AI transformation, compliance and sovereignty should accelerate your innovation, not hold you back. Google Cloud Data Boundary helps you deploy frontier AI, scale globally across commercial regions, and meet stringent regulatory requirements — with greater control and visibility over your data, your keys and your operations.

Here are six steps to get started with Data Boundary today:

  • You can access the Data Boundary directly from your Google Cloud console. Navigate to the Compliance tab in your Google Cloud console, and select Frameworks to begin with.

  • Select existing or configure your own compliance: Browse 40+ public sector, industry and sovereign AI control packages, or customize guardrails to match your specific organizational policies.

  • Select your regions: Designate precise geographic boundaries and data residency restrictions across 29 global commercial regions.

  • Evaluate workloads in dry-run mode: Enforce controls at either the folder or the project level. If you already have an active BigQuery or Gemini project running, you can turn on dry run mode to evaluate how controls behave across existing resources without disrupting live workloads.

  • Monitor against drifts and violations: Continuously track posture in real time to automatically detect non-compliant API calls and configuration drift without disrupting engineering velocity.

  • On-demand audits, scanning and compliance evidence generation: Export machine-readable evidence packages and audit-ready reports directly into your compliance workflow to accelerate Authorities to Operate (ATOs).

For a comprehensive guide on using Data Boundary, please refer to our detailed product documentation.

Nov 9 - Nov 13

A new technical guide and demo showcase how to use Apigee as an AI gateway to stack three complementary layers—deterministic static rules, semantic Google Cloud Model Armor filters, and flexible business logic via NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails. Together, they successfully intercepted 100% of benchmarked OWASP-mapped attacks without blocking safe prompts, running cheapest first to optimize performance and reduce token costs.

This end-to-end blueprint pairs GKE Custom ComputeClasses (with DWS Flex-Start and Spot fallback) and 8-NIC RoCE RDMA networking with NVIDIA NeMo RL and vLLM V1 to improve Gemma 3 mathematical reasoning accuracy.

Read thetechnical guide on Google Developer Forums and explore the reference implementation on GitHub.

    Multi-agent workloads often suffer from compounding context bloat, retry loops, and cross-agent state bleed.. Learn how to use Apigee as a model-agnostic, stateful multi-agent control plane for Google ADK and Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform workloads. By enforcing turn-0 pre-warmed caching, in-flight trace compaction, tool loop recovery, and dynamic model tiering between Gemini Flash and Frontier models, teams can achieve up to 80% net FinOps cost savings.

    Read the full article to explore reference architectures and benchmark data.

    Discover how Anthropic, creators of the Claude AI models, uses Google Cloud Pub/Sub to power their cross-cloud telemetry and billing ingestion pipeline. Facing highly variable traffic and strict security mandates, Anthropic needed a secure, serverless messaging queue with zero manual partition management. By leveraging Pub/Sub with Private Service Connect, they built a highly efficient, zero-ETL architecture capable of seamlessly handling over 1 million events per second and 500 billion daily rows. Go behind the scenes in thiscase study to learn how Anthropic reduced consumer latency by 88% and achieved sub-second end-to-end event delivery.

    Data engineering in the AI era demands fundamentally different infrastructure. Whether you're training a custom foundation model or deploying autonomous agents, you need a messaging backbone that handles bursty traffic with enterprise security and zero operational overhead. Dive into Pub/Sub’s capabilities for the AI era, reference architectures & best practices for emerging AI applications, and how Anthropic powers their telemetry pipelines with Pub/Sub inthis free on-demand webinar.

Join Nicola Cardace on Thursday, November 19, 2026, at 5:00 PM CET for a Community TechTalk exploring how to safeguard enterprise AI workloads using Model Armor. Discover practical patterns for implementing active model defense across your LLM endpoints.

    Semantic model routing replaces rigid static paths with a lightweight helper model to dynamically classify and dispatch intent-driven LLM traffic. Join Saravanakumar Rajagopal on Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 5:00 PM CET for a Community TechTalk exploring how to leverage Antigravity and skills to architect these intelligent multi-provider routing patterns natively inside Apigee. Discover how to optimize your AI infrastructure and enhance flexibility at scale.

Oct 19 - Oct 23

    Deploying an enterprise AI gateway does not require deep API or machine learning expertise. Using declarative workflows in Apigee, teams can spin up a fully governed LLM gateway in minutes using a few environment variables. Join Luis Cuellar on Thursday, October 29, 2026 for a Community TechTalk exploring end-to-end AI workflows. This update also strengthens integration with the Gemini platform, allowing you to stream responses from Gemini, Claude, and OpenAI gpt-oss models seamlessly while maintaining consistent authentication, rate limiting, and observability.

Oct 12 - Oct 16

    Scaling artificial intelligence across an enterprise requires clear token governance to keep LLM spend predictable across departments. Discover how to use Apigee to enforce isolated, tiered token budgets and model access for each team—such as assigning Engineering a dedicated budget for Gemini Pro while covering mixed usage for Marketing—without changing application code. Attendees will also gain access to a sample codebase featuring a reusable Shared Flow.

This approach provides instant feedback and zero cloud costs, helping teams speed up deployment cycles.

Discover how Apigee API Hub provides a central discovery surface to eliminate agent sprawl across tools, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and enterprise APIs. Learn how to turn existing backend services into secure MCP tools using Agent Gateway guardrails, while applying semantic caching and intelligent model routing to keep compounding token costs predictable.

    Join Google Cloud in Chicago in Oct.15 for The AI Evolution.Reserve your seat for Chicago

Discover how to use the Apigee Local Emulator and apigee-emulator-service to run sub-second assertion suites on local machines, automate CI/CD checks in GitHub Actions, and deploy ephemeral preview sandboxes on Google Cloud Run.

entries.content:
Kate Grinevskaja

Product Manager

Snigdha Jha

Product Manager

As enterprises move AI agents from experimental prototypes into production, data and platform teams are discovering that deploying an agent is only half the battle — you also need to see how it reasons, which data it touches, and what it costs to run. Today, we are announcing expanded AI agent observability and evaluation capabilities across Google Data Cloud, giving you unified visibility into your first-party (1P) data agents in BigQuery and Looker as well as custom third-party (3P) agents built with agent development frameworks such as Agent Development Kit (ADK) or LangGraph.

Putting conversational and autonomous agents into production requires solving three operational challenges: tracing multi-step reasoning while protecting sensitive data, controlling token consumption and query spend, and evaluating answer accuracy before prompt or schema changes reach users. Let’s explore how our new agent observability and evaluation capabilities help you do this.

What's new: Agent observability across Data Cloud

Running agents at scale means you need to see how they perform, what they cost, and what actions they take. We're rolling out a unified telemetry framework across Google's Agentic Data Cloud that works the same way for every agent: Capture telemetry from the agent, land it in BigQuery tables you own, and analyze it wherever your teams already work.

Unified agent observability framework capturing logging telemetry across 1P and 3P agents into BigQuery to surface performance and usage insights across developer and admin tools.

1. Capture telemetry from every first-party and custom agent

  • First-party data agents: Out-of-the-box Conversational Analytics agents emit telemetry automatically with no setup required. Queries routed to BigQuery data agents in Gemini Enterprise through agent-to-agent (A2A) workflows (now GA) send Cloud Monitoring metrics, Cloud Trace spans, and BigQuery conversation logs straight into your agent's project.

  • Custom agents: Agents built with ADK or LangGraph stream the same structured telemetry into BigQuery through single-line SDK instrumentation.

2. Land telemetry in one governed home in BigQuery

  • Conversation logging in BigQuery (GA): Managed 1P conversation logging writes to BigQuery tables you own, so you can inspect Conversational Analytics traces, including prompts and responses, directly in your data warehouse.

  • Governed by default: The Conversational Analytics API, now GA, includes always-on admin audit logs and optional data-read audit logs in Cloud Audit Logs, and supports VPC Service Controls, customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK), and regional and multi-regional data residency.

3. Analyze with dashboards wherever your teams work

  • In BigQuery (GA): Agent monitoring provides prebuilt dashboards in BigQuery Studio to track usage, active sessions, top knowledge sources, and latency across BigQuery Conversational Analytics agents.

BigQuery Conversational Analytics dashboard in BigQuery Studio, giving admins visibility into usage, active sessions, top knowledge sources, and latency.

  • In Looker (GA): System Activity dashboards for Conversational Analytics, now GA in Looker (Google Cloud core) and Looker (original), track engagement and token usage, while user ratings and query review in the Responses & feedback tab are in preview.

Looker Conversational Analytics dashboard in System Activity, giving admins visibility into usage, token consumption, and user feedback.

  • Build your own: Create interactive reports with the open-source Data Studio template or deploy the ready-made Looker Block for Agent Analytics for real-time custom agent monitoring.

Custom Data Studio dashboard built on BigQuery Agent Analytics logs to track token consumption, latency, and user engagement.

Looker Block dashboard built on BigQuery Agent Analytics telemetry to monitor session volumes, tool execution latency, and token cost distribution.

Tracing agent reasoning and protecting privacy

Enterprise observability requires balancing diagnostic telemetry with strict data privacy boundaries. Because tracking features involve ingestion and storage costs, Google Data Cloud separates operational telemetry from conversation content so admins and agent owners can govern each layer independently.

At the project or organization level, admins can enable Cloud Monitoring (aggregate metrics such as request volume, latency, and token usage) and Cloud Trace (step-by-step spans for each request) across their environment, using Cloud Trace observability scopes to consolidate telemetry across multiple agent projects. To protect sensitive data, these operational metrics and sanitized first-party trace spans exclude customer core content (such as user prompts, model responses, internal thoughts, and generated SQL).

When you need deeper transcript auditing, agent owners and editors can opt in to conversation logging on a per-agent basis:

  • Governed conversation logging in BigQuery: When enabled, a Google-managed service agent streams user prompts, responses, and turn-level telemetry into a customer-owned BigQuery table (

    agent_events
    ) via the BigQuery Storage Write API, inheriting your dataset's IAM permissions, CMEK, and VPC Service Controls. Built-in privacy guardrails enforce a fail-closed check before each turn — skipping logging whenever a knowledge source uses row-level security, column-level policy tags, or dynamic data masking — while fail-open execution keeps your users' chat sessions uninterrupted if a logging error occurs.

  • Full trace trees for custom 3P agents: While 1P conversation logging intentionally strips low-level tool arguments and internal SQL, developers building custom agents on ADK or LangGraph can instrument their code with the open-source ADK plugin (

    BigQueryAgentAnalyticsPlugin
    ). With a single-line setup, the SDK streams full tool-invocation execution trees, time-series telemetry, and multimodal payloads straight into BigQuery.

  • In-warehouse root cause and drift analysis: Because conversation logs land natively in your 

    agent_events
    table, you don't need separate export pipelines to diagnose failures. You can run BigQuery AI functions (such as 
    AI.GENERATE
    to summarize error patterns and 
    AI.EMBED
    with 
    VECTOR_SEARCH
    to cluster recurring issues) or use the open-source 
    bigquery-agent-analytics
    Python SDK and Colab starter notebook for post-hoc semantic drift clustering and LLM-as-a-judge sentiment analysis.

Controlling token costs with FinOps guardrails

As agent adoption grows, FinOps and platform teams need clear visibility into consumption alongside active controls to prevent runaway spend. With promotional trial pricing currently available for Conversational Analytics, now is a good time to establish baseline usage and cost guardrails:

  • Granular token and latency tracking: In BigQuery conversation logs, each turn records input, output, thought, cached, and total token counts alongside total turn latency, while Looker System Activity reports estimated input and output tokens across your business intelligence (BI) workloads.

  • Turnkey observability dashboards: You can track projected token usage and engagement in the BigQuery Studio Monitoring tab and native Looker System Activity dashboards, or query 

    agent_events
    log data via BigQuery SQL using the open-source seven-page Data Studio report template and self-hosted Streamlit app in the BigQuery Agent Analytics GitHub repository.

  • Active query and token spend caps: To prevent unexpected charges before they happen, you can configure per-query BigQuery byte scan caps (

    big_query_max_billed_bytes
    ) on your agent, which use dry-run estimates to block oversized queries without incurring on-demand scan charges. For BigQuery and the Conversational Analytics API, you can also enforce daily input and output token quotas (in preview) per project, user, or agent in the Google Cloud console and 
    gcloud
    CLI.

Evaluating and benchmarking your AI agents

Runtime observability works alongside systematic evaluation. While logs and traces tell you how an agent behaved in production, evaluation benchmarks verify whether updates to your prompts, models, or data schemas improve SQL accuracy and answer quality before users experience a regression:

  • Benchmarking with Prism: Our open-source evaluation tool, Prism, lets you test Conversational Analytics agents grounded in BigQuery tables or Looker Explores via the Conversational Analytics API using reusable test suites, regex assertions, and multi-region agent discovery (deployed behind an access layer such as Cloud IAP).

  • Unified evaluation and production analytics: Prism can stream completed evaluation runs directly into day-partitioned BigQuery tables in your project, placing your pre-deployment benchmark scores right alongside your production 

    agent_events
    logs for side-by-side analysis in BigQuery and Looker.

  • Native BigQuery evaluations: First-party agent evaluations in BigQuery (built on the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform evaluation service with bring-your-own-service-account support) are available in preview via API and a guided Colab notebook.

Getting started

Ready to bring visibility, governance, and cost control to your AI agents? Here is how to get started in three steps:

  • Enable first-party agent observability. Turn on Cloud Monitoring and Cloud Trace in your project and opt in to per-agent conversation logging using the BigQuery agent monitoring guide, and track BI token consumption with the Looker Conversational Analytics overview and Looker System Activity documentation.

  • Instrument custom agents and deploy analytics dashboards. Add the BigQuery Agent Analytics SDK to your ADK or LangGraph agents, launch the open-source Data Studio report template or Streamlit app, and explore in-warehouse log analysis with the Colab starter notebook.

  • Benchmark your agents and set cost guardrails. Run automated accuracy suites with Prism, and configure BigQuery byte scan caps and daily token quotas via Manage BigQuery costs for agents.

entries.content:
Megan Gawlik

Product Manager, HPC

Annie Ma-Weaver

Group Product Manager, HPC

Computational scientists and HPC engineers have always been among the earliest adopters of new computing paradigms, and agents are no exception. Today, research and engineering teams use AI models and agents for things such as ingesting dense scientific literature, optimizing code, and autonomously steering simulations.

Yet moving from an agent that suggests code optimizations to an agentic system that reliably architects, provisions, and optimizes production HPC workloads at scale takes more than a general-purpose reasoning model. Without deep infrastructure and domain context, an unguided agent can still pair incompatible storage tiers with compute-optimized VMs, overlook placement policies, or stall when diagnosing a multi-node MPI fabric error.

That challenge led our team to ask a simple question: What if we could package our deep HPC and scientific expertise into reusable agent skills, turning complex setup and optimization into guided workflows?

At SC26, we are showing how Google Cloud brings agentic HPC to life with reusable skills that teach agents how to build and run HPC workloads. In addition, we’re also demonstrating evolutionary agents that optimize your algorithms at cloud scale, and purpose-built supercomputing infrastructure designed for where HPC meets AI.

Teaching agents to speak HPC: From blueprints to skills

Organizations rely on Cluster Toolkit to deploy repeatable, production-ready HPC environments on Google Cloud through declarative YAML blueprints. Now we are expanding these capabilities by pairing Cluster Toolkit with composable agent skills with self-describing, deterministic tools, validated through automated, end-to-end testing and available for download from the Google Skills and DeepMind Science Skills repositories. Together, this delivers:

  • Infrastructure skills that validate before they deploy: When you ask an agent to stand up a cluster, the skill directs it to first audit your compute and storage quotas, run rapid canary checks for regional capacity, match your workload to a validated Cluster Toolkit blueprint, and wait for human approval, all before running the gcluster deploy command.

  • Workload-specific skills that know the science: After your cluster is live, domain skills connected to Google Skills and DeepMind Science Skills guide the agent through things like configuring OpenFOAM and Siemens STAR-CCM+ fluid dynamics runs, tuning GROMACS and AlphaFold 3 life-sciences pipelines, or launching Devito and Open Porous Media (OPM) subsurface simulations with browser-based 3D visualization.

  • Built-in governance and Day-2 diagnostics: Agents operate inside strict IAM, Kueue quota, and budget guardrails, with full provenance in Cloud Logging and structured troubleshooting skills (gke-kueue-debugging) to resolve stuck queues or node drains automatically.

Scaling from local prototype to breakthrough code

Configuring and running existing solvers is only part of the discovery loop. Across financial services, electronic design automation (EDA), manufacturing, logistics, pharmaceuticals, and AI training, competitive advantage comes from having the fastest underlying code and algorithms. Historically, squeezing out performance gains required scarce optimization specialists and costly brute-force compute.

Developed by Google DeepMind, AlphaEvolve changes the equation by using a Gemini-powered evolutionary loop to iteratively mutate, benchmark, and optimize code and 3D engineering parameters against target metrics. The AlphaEvolve on Cloud Batch solution,  streamlines the process of moving from a seed algorithm on a laptop to massive parallel experimentation. With Batch, you get:

  • Automated parallel evaluation: A single gcluster blueprint provisions the AlphaEvolve controller environment and uses Batch to fan out hundreds of candidate evaluations concurrently across single-VM sandboxes or multi-node MPI task groups.

  • Interactive control from your preferred surface: Researchers can steer evolutionary experiments and inspect candidate lineage through hosted Python notebooks, or integrate optimization runs directly into their existing CLI workloads and agent-driven development tools.

  • Evaluation at production scale: Evolving an algorithm on a single node with slow networking risks producing code that only performs well at small scale. By evaluating candidates across Google Cloud compute instances with Cloud RDMA and Google Cloud Managed Lustre — and using Spot VMs or Dynamic Workload Scheduler (DWS) to balance cost against turnaround time — you discover algorithms tuned for real supercomputing fabrics, permanently lowering the compute cost of every future production run.

Supercomputing infrastructure under the hood

An autonomous workflow is only as capable as the infrastructure beneath it. As agentic pipelines pivot dynamically between memory-bandwidth-bound physics solvers, domain foundation models (like AlphaFold 3, AlphaGenome, and WeatherNext), and large-scale AI training, Google Cloud provides a unified hardware and orchestration fabric managed by Cluster Director that offers:

  • Tightly coupled HPC and scale-out compute: Run classic MPI simulations on H4D instances powered by 5th Gen AMD EPYC processors and Cloud RDMA, including 3 TB high-memory shapes built for large EDA and engineering models. Alternatively, you can maximize performance-per-watt on Arm-based C4A instances powered by Google Axion.

  • Next-generation GPU acceleration: Run coupled physics-AI pipelines and multi-node GPU simulations on A4 and A4X instances (NVIDIA Blackwell B200 and GB200 NVL72), scale frontier AI training and reasoning on newly available A5X bare metal instances built on the NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 platform, and use G4 instances with NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs to accelerate CAE, CFD, and 3D visualization while reducing per-core software licensing costs.

  • 8th gen TPUs for the agentic era: Deploy 8th generation TPUs, featuring TPU 8t for large-scale pre-training, reinforcement learning, and accelerated mathematical modeling and simulation (ModSim), alongside TPU 8i for high-throughput, low-latency reasoning and agentic inference. Additionally, Batch now supports running jobs on single-host TPU slices, providing flexible provisioning options for accelerated HPC and AI/ML workloads.

  • Sub-millisecond parallel storage: Reduce data bottlenecks between simulation and AI stages with Google Cloud Managed Lustre, delivering up to 10 TB/s of read throughput, GPUDirect Storage over RDMA, and an 80 PB Dynamic Tier with Cloud Storage Mirroring. For even more performance, you can pair it with Cloud Storage FUSE local SSD caching.

Experience it live at SC26 in Chicago

Agentic HPC is not about turning unguided models loose on a terminal. This shift is about combining the reasoning power of Gemini with the codified engineering of Cluster Toolkit skills, evolutionary optimization on Batch, and purpose-built supercomputing hardware — so your teams spend their time on discovery rather than infrastructure plumbing.

Visiting SC26 (November 15–20)? Stop by Booth #3418 at McCormick Place West for live demos of Antigravity for HPC, the HPC Prompt Playground, and AlphaEvolve for HPC, and join us at our Advanced Computing Community Half-Day Workshop and Agentic and Hybrid HPC Birds of a Feather (BoF) session.

To start building today, explore the Google Cloud Cluster Toolkit and Google Cloud HPC solutions. To access and implement these agentic workflows, download the validated templates from the Google Skills and DeepMind Science Skills repositories.
